episodes.178308: A strong thunderstorm pushing offshore of the St Lucie County coast produced severe hail.
episodes.178310: A thunderstorm along the Treasure Coast produced an early morning waterspout, with an afternoon thunderstorm producing strong to severe wind gusts along the Brevard Coast.
episodes.178388: Afternoon storms produce severe hail in Hillsborough and Polk counties, the largest up to 3 inches in diameter in Hillsborough County, and winds downing a tree onto a structure in Sumter County.
episodes.179737: On April 24th, a minor shortwave trough funneled plentiful moisture into the region. This allowed for numerous scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms to bring localized flooding from the rainfall and locally gusty winds, especially in the eastern metro of South Florida throughout the day.
episodes.179763: Significant flooding occurred on the mainstem Mississippi largely due to the record snowfall this winter in Minnesota and Wisconsin, frozen ground, rapid snowmelt during the middle of April, and saturated soils.  Major flooding was observed at all sites along the Mississippi north of Keokuk Iowa and most sites saw one of their top 10 crests on record.|This flooding had numerous impacts, with many roads, businesses, homes, and people affected.

events.narrative: Airport personnel at the Treasure Coast International Airport (KFPR) reported a waterspout approximately 10 miles east-southeast of the airport. The spout lasted about 4 minutes.

A local broadcast media meteorologist shared photos of flooding via social media. Heavy rainfall from a thunderstorm caused flooding and road closures in portions of NE 191st Street, from NE 29th Ave to Biscayne Boulevard in Aventura. Rainfall estimates of 2 to 3 inches in just one to two hours were received in the vicinity.

The Mississippi River at Rock Island Lock and Dam 15 rose above its major flood stage of 18.0 feet around mid day on  April 24th and continued to rise to its crest of 21.41 on the evening of April 30th.
